Overhaul:
   This software is aptly named, as it allows you to create characters based on the layering of pre-generated images, similar to how one creates a character/plays dress--up with paper dolls. The characters you can create, the backgrounds you can use depends on the dlc package(s) you have purchased; either via Steam, through their website, or claimed for free by earning certain in-app achievements.

Pros:
-Easy to use. It is all "point & click" interface."
-You  can earn free dlc packages by completing certain in-app achievements.
-Some dlc packages are of non-Human characters.
-While the game supports "Fantasy" and "Modern" genre character creation, you are not locked-in to just using items from one genre to create your character.

Cons-
-You need to sign up/have an account on the software's website if you want to claim your free dlc packages.
-Imo, there are not enough non-Human characters templates to build upon, when compared to Human templates.
-A slight learning curve, when it comes to  layering clothing, visual effects, and exporting created characters as a finished image.

Ultimate Review:
-ePic Generator is worth purchasing, if you are an individual that creators characters, either for a fanfic, an rpg, a full-blown novel, or just for yourself, but are not able to commission artwork of them, or are having difficulty in visualizing their appearance.

This software tool is very good, even at its substantial price point. The recent addition of Mac compatibility [01/2022] adds even more to its value. The main criticism you hear about this software is the price of the DLC content. I assure you, if you buy it on sale you have nothing to complain about. I paid full price for The Pro Version, the PSD export feature, and a few outfit packs. Over time I bought the entire expansion library.

We're spoiled by the mindset that becomes common when platforms like Blender and Unity are free to use. But if you were already skilled with those programs you wouldn't be looking at ECG. You are paying for ease of use. If you think it isn't feature rich enough, the PSD export option will allow your digital artistic skill to go where you want. 

I'm old enough to have bought programs like this at a place we used to call Shopping Malls that had stores that sold "Computer Software". Lots of programs promise any At-Home user with the skills of a child could produce a professional comic book or other finished consumer product. It's no more true today than it was then. 
Whether you spend $20 on a few outfit packs for this game or $100 for the pro options the price would have been the same for the same amount of features back then. So you're basically getting this game for a late 1990's price. The only difference is back then you would have had to install it off of 9 CD Roms, and it would have been un-returnable the minute you opened the box. 

Look anywhere on the internet and you'll spend the same amount of money on a starter pack of assets for any 2D or 3D platform. That's what this is. ePic Character Generator is the Magix Music Maker of character art; If you were a real DJ you wouldn't need it.

I absolutely LOVE this software! Developing an online RPG and needing appropriate images for the game, I've used this software over the course of six years now and continue to use it on a weekly basis. The artwork is beautiful, I can mix and match just about anything I wish, and I can even import individual layers into Photoshop. I've also communicated with the developers of the software on numerous occasions; they always got back to me within 24 hours and were both sincere and helpful.

I have played around with this software for a year and invested somewhere around $100 into upgrades and asset packs. While it is possible to make some pleasing assets, I cannot recommend this application because of several functional deficiencies.

1)	You cannot combine assets from different seasons, not even assets which do not rely on a character fit (e.g. companions, held objects, set pieces, atmospheric effects). While this makes partial sense for clothing (i.e. tailored for specific forms and postures) this doesn't make sense for most accessories (e.g. pouch, sword)
2)	You cannot resize or rotate objects (e.g. companions). This is mainly an issue for set pieces and effects rather than clothing, but several objects that look good in the pack are actually too massive to make use of and there is virtually nothing you can do about it.
3)	You cannot export images as PNG layers without the PSD exporter. Because of how the application works, it should be trivial to export a character as a collection of layers, doing so would allow the user to manually mix clothing from seasons or resize companion, addressing issues 1 and 2.

The developer knows about issues 1 & 2 and has done nothing to address them. His solution is just pay an extra $30.

In a very real sense, if you want to make characters without a watermark, who aren’t locked into specific (undergarments with prominent straps), with assets that you can resize (via PNG layers) you will need to spend ~$70 (e.g. pro and PSD exporter), and even then you be forced to manually splice together elements from different seasons.  

The punchline here is that the tool is built with defects (most unintentional, some intentional) that will prevent you from making full use of the assets you’ve purchased (e.g. cross set, resizing). Rather than working to address these issues (modifying the application) the developer asks you to just pay more, by treating functional improvements as paid expansions.

[h1]Creative and Visual[/h1]

This is not a game per se, but a software tool for character generation, as the name says. It provides the ability to not only create fully customized characters, but to export them as images, cards, or tokens. This makes the opportunities for use almost endless. Whether you're interested in visualizing characters for your own creative writing, or for your tabletop games, or simply for illustration purposes; the generator  is a great visual creativity outlet. I get many hours enjoyment in-game and out of game from the materials and characters.

I tried the free version first, just to see if it had enough to make it worth the expense. I was pleased with all of the content, and wanted to remove the logo from my characters, as well as to export full size images. So, I bought the pro version and am adding packs as possible. I recommend the generator pro version for anyone who is looking for creative and open-ended 'games' and software. After all, not all games have to be linear. You know what you want, and the ePic Character Generator allows you to do as you wish. 

One suggestion for the software devs that I would like to see added to the Pro version, perhaps, is the ability to be able to re-pose the characters. Any flexibility at all in character posing would be a good addition.

This product alone has made my life way easier. If I need a character for a campaign I can just create them here pretty quick. I really enjoy how easy it is to create characters and they have a large selection of characters.  They are still releasing new characters and improving the software.
